newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Maxtel plunges as market digests results.
newsitem.headline: Maxtel plunges as market digests results.

text.p: Shares in South African telecommunications equipment suppplier Maxtel Ltd plunged 30.43 pecent on Thursday as the market digested a recent poor set of results, dealers said.
Maxtel shares fell by 70 cents to 160 cents, or 30.43 percent, the highest percentage fall on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange by lunch recess.
"It is just that they had bad results. I don't know why guys pushed it so high in the first place," one dealer said.
Maxtel's year high was 340 cents, but on October 4 it posted results for the 16 months to June 30 that disappointed the market.
The group made saw a decline in attributable earnings per share to 1.7 cents from 5.1 after unexpected delays from several major suppliers hit profts.
But dealers said there was some demand for the stock coming in at lower levels and predicted the shares would recover some of their lost ground in the afternoon.
"It looks a bargain at these levels," one said.

Maxtel recently secured a deal to get a new joint-owner. Telular South Africa, which currently owns 71 percent of the group, has agreed to sell 2.67 million shares to Midland-Molefe Property Group Ltd for 2.4 million rand
Midland-Molefe is to change its name to Lehlabile Investment Co Ltd (LIC). The deal will see LIC hold 33.3 percent of Maxtel and Telular retain 37.7 percent.
The new owners intend to extend a rights offer to shareholders to raise cash for new ventures in broadcasting, telecommunications, electronics and information systems.
Dealers said it was too early, and the plans were too vague, to say if the proposed rights issue would be hit by the share price drop.
